subject: Clarifying DPA / subprocessors language for hosted API & console
messages:
From: Dana Ruiz <dana.ruiz@datatrust.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@fintechco.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifying DPA/subprocessor phrasing for hosted API

Hi Marissa,

Quick follow-up from our legal team after reviewing the draft DPA you shared last week. Two asks they flagged that we need clearer public-facing text for before counsel will sign:

1) Subprocessor disclosure: they want a short sentence we can show to our procurement team that explains how Redwood notifies customers of subprocessors and the cadence of updates (e.g., "we publish an up-to-date list and notify customers 30 days before material changes").

2) International transfers: they need explicit language around whether Redwood relies on SCCs, adequacy decisions, or other transfer mechanisms for hosted API traffic from EU-origin data. If SCCs are used, can you confirm whether those apply at the contract level or via a platform-wide policy?

Also, Samir asked whether the Console's "Data Processing" page should be updated with a short paragraph or a link to the DPA.

Can you point us to the canonical wording you intend to publish (privacy policy or console text) so we can circulate it internally?

Thanks — Dana
DataTrust Legal

--
Attachment: none

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarifying DPA/subprocessor phrasing for hosted API

Dana — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Neha (Legal) and Vivek (Security & Compliance) to confirm the precise public-facing language and transfer mechanisms.

Short answer up front: Redwood will provide an up-to-date subprocessor list and a 30-day notice window for material additions; for transfers we rely on SCCs for controller-processor flows and on adequacy decisions where they exist. I’ve asked Legal to produce a few short candidate sentences we can publish on the Console Data Processing page and in the privacy center.

Next steps: Neha/Vivek — can you confirm and share a 2–3 line copy for both the Console and the Privacy Center by Monday? Dana/Samir — I’ll attach the latest DPA and subprocessor list as soon as Legal signs off.

Best,
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 13 Sep 2025 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Draft wording for Console + Privacy Center (DPA/subprocessors/transfers)

Team — Dana at DataTrust wants crisp, consumer-facing language so their procurement and security teams can sign off quickly. Below are three candidate snippets; feedback requested. We should produce both a Console-ready line (short) and a Privacy Center paragraph (slightly longer).

Console (short, <180 chars) — option A/B/C:
- Option A: "We maintain an up-to-date list of subprocessors and provide at least 30 days’ notice for material changes."
- Option B: "Redwood publishes our subprocessors and gives customers 30 days’ notice before major additions; details in our DPA."
- Option C: "Subprocessors are listed publicly; customers will be notified 30 days in advance of material changes and may object per the DPA."

Privacy Center (paragraph) — focus points:
- Redwood acts as a processor for hosted API requests; we process data under customer instructions as set out in the DPA.
- Subprocessors: we publish a current list and provide 30 days' notice for material changes; customers can review and raise objections during that period.
- International transfers: we rely on EU Commission adequacy decisions where applicable and Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for controller-processor transfers; SCCs are implemented at the contract level (in the DPA) and applied platform-wide for hosted API traffic.

Open questions for Legal/security:
- Do we want the Console copy to reference the DPA explicitly ("see DPA") or just say "details in Privacy Center"?
- Any regulated wording Vivek wants to add around logs/audit retention?

Laura — if Sales Ops needs a different tack for enterprise docs (longer multi-sentence copy), flag and we’ll produce a separate template.

Thanks — please reply with suggested edits.

-Marissa

--

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Sep 2025 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Draft wording for Console + Privacy Center (DPA/subprocessors/transfers)

On Sat, Sep 13, 2025 at 10:15 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team — Dana at DataTrust wants crisp, consumer-facing language so their procurement and security teams can sign off quickly. Below are three candidate snippets; feedback requested.

Thanks Marissa — good starter options. I made edits inline and attached the signed DPA, current subprocessors list, and SCC summary for your review. Key legal points (short):

- Processor role: confirm we are "processor" for hosted API customers. That stays as-is.
- Subprocessor notice: publish list + 30 days notice for material changes is acceptable. Suggest the Console line be: "We publish our subprocessors and provide at least 30 days’ notice for material changes (see DPA for details)."
- Transfers: we rely on adequacy decisions where present; otherwise we incorporate SCCs at the contract level and make SCCs available to customers via the DPA and export controls page. Note: SCCs are implemented by contract; we do not re-execute SCCs per-tenant but the DPA incorporates them by reference and we provide a signed appendix when required.

Recommended Privacy Center paragraph (final):
"Redwood acts as a processor for Hosted API customers. We publish an up-to-date list of subprocessors and provide at least 30 days’ notice for material changes; customers may review and object to new subprocessors in accordance with the DPA. For international transfers, Redwood relies on applicable EU Commission adequacy decisions and, where necessary, Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) incorporated in the DPA. Customers requiring a separate SCC execution or additional transfer mechanisms can request a signed appendix via Sales or Legal."

I’ve attached: redwood-dpa-v3.pdf (final), subprocessors-2025-09.csv, sccs-signed.pdf.

If everyone is ok, Marissa — please send Dana the DPA and snippets and mark the Console copy as "temporary" until we push the privacy center update.

-Neha

--
Attachments: redwood-dpa-v3.pdf (application/pdf); subprocessors-2025-09.csv (text/csv); sccs-signed.pdf (application/pdf)
